children.title: Inexact Proximal Subproblems
children.top_down_role: Approximate proximal solves organized by residual or objective-accuracy criteria.

knowledge_statements.title: Inexact Proximal Subproblems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines verifiable absolute and relative accuracy conditions for a tangent proximal solve.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m_k:T_{x_k}\mathcal M\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be a proper lower-semicontinuous proximal model with minimum value \(m_k^*\), and let \(\eta_k\) be an approximate minimizer. An absolute value-error condition is \[m_k(\eta_k)-m_k^*\le\varepsilon_k,\qquad \varepsilon_k\ge0.\] When a computable residual \(r_k\in\partial m_k(\eta_k)\) is available, a relative residual condition is \[\|r_k\|_{x_k}\le \sigma_k\|\eta_k\|_{x_k},\qquad 0\le\sigma_k<1.\] An outer convergence theorem must state which condition it uses and whether the sequences \((\varepsilon_k)\) or \((\sigma_k)\) must be summable, vanishing, or uniformly bounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inexact tangent proximal solve should satisfy a declared objective-gap or subgradient-residual tolerance whose iterationwise regime matches the outer convergence theorem.
assumptions_latex: \(m_k\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and attains its minimum.
The selected generalized subdifferential \(\partial m_k\) is declared when residual accuracy is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Accept \(\eta_k\) only if the chosen absolute-gap or relative-residual inequality holds with its prescribed accuracy regime.

notation.meaning: Minimum value of the kth tangent proximal model.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition content kind fits the inexact-subproblem leaf, and the objective-gap condition is precise. The residual condition depends materially on the chosen generalized subdifferential and scaling, while the summable, vanishing, or bounded regimes depend on the outer theorem; no source is supplied to validate these choices.

children.title: Semismooth Proximal Subproblems
children.top_down_role: Structured nonsmooth subproblems amenable to semismooth local solvers.

knowledge_statements.title: Semismooth Proximal Subproblems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semismooth Newton solution of a tangent-space proximal optimality equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a Riemannian manifold \(\mathcal M\), \(x\in\mathcal M\), stepsize \(t>0\), smooth \(f\), and proper lower-semicontinuous \(g\), define \(q_x(\eta)=\langle \operatorname{grad}f(x),\eta\rangle+\frac{1}{2t}\lVert\eta\rVert^2+g(R_x(\eta))\) on \(T_x\mathcal M\). Express its stationarity condition as a locally Lipschitz residual \(F_x(\eta)=0\). Starting from \(\eta_0\), choose \(V_j\in\partial_C F_x(\eta_j)\), solve \(V_js_j=-F_x(\eta_j)\), and set \(\eta_{j+1}=\eta_j+s_j\), with globalization if required. Stop when \(\lVert F_x(\eta_j)\rVert\leq\varepsilon\), and return \(\eta_j\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve the tangent proximal model by semismooth Newton steps applied to a generalized stationarity residual, terminating when its norm meets the prescribed tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(R_x\) is a retraction defined near the origin of \(T_x\mathcal M\).
\(F_x\) is locally Lipschitz and semismooth near a solution.
Selected generalized Jacobians are nonsingular near that solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\eta_j\) is an \(\varepsilon\)-stationary approximate solution of the proximal subproblem.

notation.meaning: Clarke generalized Jacobian of the residual

review_flags: Exact manifold semismooth-Newton formulation requires an authoritative source.
The supplied locator hints do not support this specialized claim.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits the leaf, but no source or inspectable locator supports this manifold semismooth-Newton formulation. In particular, existence and local Lipschitzness of the residual, its relation to stationarity of the retraction-composed model, and the generalized-Jacobian assumptions are framework-dependent.

children.title: Inner-Solve Accuracy Regimes
children.top_down_role: Fixed, diminishing, plus adaptive accuracy choices for proximal subproblems.

knowledge_statements.title: Inner-Solve Accuracy Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Absolute, summable, and relative stopping rules for inexact tangent proximal solves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r_k\) be a computable stationarity residual for the tangent proximal subproblem and let \(G_k\) be the outer proximal-gradient mapping. Standard admissible regimes include: absolute accuracy, \(\lVert r_k\rVert\leq\varepsilon_k\) with \(\varepsilon_k\to0\); summable accuracy, \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\varepsilon_k<\infty\); and relative accuracy, \(\lVert r_k\rVert\leq\theta_k\lVert G_k\rVert\) with \(0\leq\theta_k\leq\bar\theta<1\). A forcing regime may additionally require \(\theta_k\to0\) to preserve a faster local outer rate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inner solves may use vanishing absolute errors, summable errors, or residuals uniformly proportional to the current outer stationarity measure.
assumptions_latex: \(r_k\) vanishes exactly at a solution of the inner optimality system.
\(G_k\) is a valid outer stationarity measure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed inequalities define progressively stronger accuracy controls for the inexact inner solves.
review_flags: A source is needed to align these regimes with the intended manifold proximal-gradient framework.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role fits the leaf and the regimes are plausible, but no source establishes that these residual criteria are admissible for the intended manifold proximal-gradient method or that the listed regimes are progressively stronger without additional relations among the tolerances.

children.title: Generalized-Derivative Geometry
children.top_down_role: Tangent-compatible generalized derivative structure relevant to semismooth solves.

knowledge_statements.title: Generalized-Derivative Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Intrinsic generalized derivatives obtained by transporting nearby tangent-space derivatives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be a locally Lipschitz vector field on a Riemannian manifold \(\mathcal M\), and fix \(x\in\mathcal M\). For differentiability points \(x_i\to x\), transport the covariant derivatives back to \(T_x\mathcal M\). The intrinsic Clarke generalized covariant derivative is represented by \[\partial_C F(x)=\operatorname{co}\left\{\lim_{i\to\infty}\mathcal T_{x_i\to x}\circ\nabla F(x_i)\circ\mathcal T_{x\to x_i}: x_i\to x,\ F\text{ differentiable at }x_i\right\},\] whenever the displayed limits exist, where closure may be included in infinite-dimensional settings.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The intrinsic Clarke derivative is the convex hull of limiting nearby covariant derivatives after all operators are transported to one tangent space.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal M\) is finite-dimensional and equipped with a compatible local transport.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\partial_C F(x)\) is a set of endomorphisms of the single space \(T_x\mathcal M\).

notation.meaning: local vector transport from the tangent space at y to that at x
covariant derivative of F at y

review_flags: Transport conventions and closure requirements vary across intrinsic generalized-derivative definitions.
The supplied sources do not establish this representation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation role fits the leaf, but the formula depends on a precise transport convention, differentiability notion, and closure convention. A generic compatible local vector transport does not by itself establish that the resulting set is an intrinsic Clarke generalized covariant derivative.

knowledge_statements.title: Composite-Stationarity Convergence Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cluster-point stationarity for descent-type Riemannian proximal-gradient iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=f+g\) be bounded below on a finite-dimensional Riemannian manifold, with \(f\) continuously differentiable and \(g\) proper and lower semicontinuous. Suppose iterates satisfy \(x_{k+1}=R_{x_k}(\eta_k)\), remain in a compact set, and obey \[F(x_k)-F(x_{k+1})\geq c\lVert G_{t_k}(x_k)\rVert^2,\qquad \lVert\eta_k\rVert\leq C\lVert G_{t_k}(x_k)\rVert,\] for constants \(c,C>0\). If the proximal optimality residual is consistent with the limiting subdifferential, then \(\lVert G_{t_k}(x_k)\rVert\to0\), and every cluster point \(x_\star\) satisfies \(0\in\operatorname{grad}f(x_\star)+\partial g(x_\star)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sufficient decrease, compactness, and a consistent proximal residual force the stationarity measure to vanish and make every accumulation point composite-stationary.
assumptions_latex: The stepsizes \(t_k\) stay in a compact subinterval of \((0,\infty)\).
The retraction and subdifferential model are locally consistent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert G_{t_k}(x_k)\rVert\to0\) and \(0\in\operatorname{grad}f(x_\star)+\partial g(x_\star)\) at every cluster point.
review_flags: The precise stationarity-transfer hypotheses depend on the selected manifold composite model.
No supplied locator directly supports this theorem.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem role fits the convergence-family container. The descent inequality does imply vanishing mapping norms, but the phrase 'consistent with the limiting subdifferential' is not a precise hypothesis sufficient to transfer this limit to composite stationarity at every cluster point. An authoritative framework-specific theorem is required.

knowledge_statements.title: Proximal-Gradient Iteration-Complexity Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case outer-iteration bound for a squared proximal-gradient stationarity measure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume a Riemannian proximal-gradient method generates \(x_k\) and satisfies \[F(x_k)-F(x_{k+1})\geq c\lVert G_t(x_k)\rVert^2\] with \(c>0\), fixed admissible stepsize \(t>0\), and lower bound \(F_{\inf}>-\infty\). Then, after \(N\geq1\) outer iterations, \[\min_{0\leq k<N}\lVert G_t(x_k)\rVert^2\leq\frac{F(x_0)-F_{\inf}}{cN}.\] Consequently, an iterate satisfying \(\lVert G_t(x_k)\rVert\leq\varepsilon\) is obtained within at most \(\left\lceil (F(x_0)-F_{\inf})/(c\varepsilon^2)\right\rceil\) outer iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A uniform decrease proportional to the squared proximal-gradient norm yields an order epsilon-to-the-minus-two outer-iteration bound for stationarity.
assumptions_latex: Every accepted iteration satisfies the displayed uniform descent inequality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The outer-iteration complexity for \(\lVert G_t\rVert\leq\varepsilon\) is \(O(\varepsilon^{-2})\).

notation.meaning: known or theoretical lower bound on the objective

review_flags: The telescoping bound is standard, but a manifold proximal-gradient source is required for the descent premise.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound role exactly fits the leaf, and the displayed estimate follows by telescoping the assumed descent inequality. No cited source or standard-field rationale supports the manifold proximal-gradient descent premise or its stationarity mapping in this record.

children.title: Local Identification
children.top_down_role: Finite or asymptotic recognition of a locally relevant nonsmooth stratum.

knowledge_statements.title: Local Identification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite identification of a partly smooth active manifold under nondegeneracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=f+g\), where \(f\) is continuously differentiable and \(g\) is partly smooth at a composite-stationary point \(x_\star\) relative to a smooth embedded manifold \(\mathcal A\). Suppose \(x_k\to x_\star\), the proximal points satisfy \(v_k\in\partial g(x_k)\), and \(v_k\to-\operatorname{grad}f(x_\star)\). If the nondegeneracy condition \(-\operatorname{grad}f(x_\star)\in\operatorname{ri}\partial g(x_\star)\) holds, then there exists \(K<\infty\) such that \(x_k\in\mathcal A\) for every \(k\geq K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convergence, partial smoothness, and strict complementarity force proximal iterates to enter the active manifold after finitely many iterations.
assumptions_latex: \(g\) is partly smooth at \(x_\star\) relative to \(\mathcal A\).
The subgradient sequence is graph-consistent and converges as stated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists K<\infty\ \forall k\geq K:\ x_k\in\mathcal A\).

notation.meaning: active manifold of g at the limit point
selected subgradient of g at the kth iterate

review_flags: A precise intrinsic partial-smoothness identification theorem needs a supporting source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem role fits the leaf, but intrinsic finite-identification results generally require a precise partial-smoothness or identifiability framework, including the applicable regularity and graph/value convergence hypotheses. The supplied assumptions and source list do not establish the stated result.

children.title: Active Manifold Structure
children.top_down_role: Smooth local geometry exposed after identification of the active stratum.

knowledge_statements.title: Active Manifold Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Partial smoothness structure supporting active-set identification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A proper lower-semicontinuous function \(g:\mathcal M\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is partly smooth at \(x_\star\) relative to an embedded manifold \(\mathcal A\subset\mathcal M\) when: \(g|_{\mathcal A}\) is smooth near \(x_\star\); the subdifferential mapping \(\partial g\) is continuous along \(\mathcal A\) at \(x_\star\); and the sharpness relation \[T_{x_\star}\mathcal A=\bigl(\operatorname{par}\partial g(x_\star)\bigr)^\perp\] holds after identifying cotangent and tangent spaces by the Riemannian metric. Then \(\mathcal A\) is an active manifold for \(g\) at \(x_\star\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An active manifold is a smooth restriction of a nonsmooth function whose tangent space matches the orthogonal complement of subgradient variation.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal M\) is a finite-dimensional Riemannian manifold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal A\) locally captures the smooth stratum and sharp nonsmooth geometry of \(g\) at \(x_\star\).

notation.meaning: linear subspace parallel to the affine hull of C
tangent space of the active manifold

review_flags: Definitions of partial smoothness differ in regularity and prox-regularity requirements.
An authoritative manifold-specific definition is needed.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition role fits the leaf, but definitions of partial smoothness differ on subdifferential regularity, prox-regularity, continuity, and sharpness assumptions. No authoritative manifold-specific source identifies the stated three conditions as a complete definition.

children.title: Post-Identification Dynamics
children.top_down_role: Local behavior after iterates remain on the identified structure.

assumptions_latex: The active manifold is identified in finitely many iterations.
The induced map \(T_{\mathcal A}\) is continuously differentiable near \(x_\star\) and satisfies \(T_{\mathcal A}(x_\star)=x_\star\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(q\in(\rho(DT_{\mathcal A}(x_\star)),1)\), there are a neighborhood \(U\) of \(x_\star\) in \(\mathcal A\) and a constant \(C_q>0\) such that an orbit starting in \(U\) satisfies \(d(x_k,x_\star)\leq C_q q^{k-K}d(x_K,x_\star)\) for all \(k\geq K\).

notation.meaning: post-identification update restricted to the active manifold

review_flags: An algorithm-specific source is still required for the induced smooth map and its local rate.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth local fixed-point dynamics after finite active-manifold identification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume a proximal-gradient sequence identifies an active manifold \(\mathcal A\) at iteration \(K\), and thereafter has the form \(x_{k+1}=T_{\mathcal A}(x_k)\) on \(\mathcal A\). Let \(x_\star\in\mathcal A\) satisfy \(T_{\mathcal A}(x_\star)=x_\star\), and suppose \(T_{\mathcal A}\) is continuously differentiable near \(x_\star\). If \(\rho(DT_{\mathcal A}(x_\star))<1\), then \(x_\star\) is a locally linearly attracting fixed point. More precisely, for every \(q\in(\rho(DT_{\mathcal A}(x_\star)),1)\), sufficiently close initial points generate iterates satisfying \(d(x_k,x_\star)\leq C_q q^{k-K}d(x_K,x_\star)\) for some \(C_q>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After identification, the method is a smooth fixed-point iteration on the active manifold. If the stationary point is a fixed point and the derivative there has spectral radius below one, nearby iterates converge locally linearly.
knowledge_statements.title: Post-Identification Dynamics

children.title: Identification Failure Boundary
children.top_down_role: Degeneracy, inexactness, or geometric mismatch obstructing stable active-structure recognition.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_k=(1-t)^kx_0\to0\), but \(x_k\notin\{0\}\) for every finite \(k\).
review_flags: The corrected counterexample is directly checkable but still lacks an authoritative source locator.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of finite identification when relative-interior nondegeneracy is lost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Finite identification is not guaranteed if \(-\operatorname{grad}f(x_\star)\notin\operatorname{ri}\partial g(x_\star)\). For the Euclidean composite objective \(F(x)=\frac12(x-1)^2+|x|\) and proximal-gradient stepsize \(t\in(0,1)\), the stationary point is \(x_\star=0\), while \(-f'(0)=1\in\partial|\cdot|(0)=[-1,1]\) lies on the boundary. From any \(x_0>0\), the update satisfies \(x_{k+1}=(1-t)x_k>0\); hence \(x_k\to0\) but no finite iterate enters the active manifold \(\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At boundary complementarity, proximal-gradient iterates can converge to the active point forever without identifying its zero-dimensional manifold.
knowledge_statements.title: Identification Failure Boundary

children.title: Inexactness Failure Boundary
children.top_down_role: Persistent inner-solve error, weak accuracy control, plus accumulated approximation effects.

knowledge_statements.title: Inexactness Failure Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Persistent inner error can prevent convergence to exact composite stationarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(F(x)=\frac12x^2\) on \(\mathbb R\) and an inexact gradient-proximal update \(x_{k+1}=x_k-t(x_k+e_k)\) with \(t\in(0,2)\). If the inner error is constant, \(e_k\equiv e\neq0\), then \[x_k=(1-t)^kx_0-e\bigl(1-(1-t)^k\bigr)\longrightarrow-e.\] Thus the iterates converge, but the limit has stationarity residual \(|F'(-e)|=|e|>0\). Vanishing, summable, or suitably relative errors are therefore essential when exact stationarity rather than convergence to an error neighborhood is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonvanishing inner error biases even a stable quadratic iteration toward a nonstationary point, showing why accuracy must improve.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_k\to-e\neq0\), so the method fails to reach the unique stationary point \(0\).
review_flags: The example is elementary and verifiable, but no supplied source locator supports it.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits and the scalar recurrence is algebraically correct. However, no citation or standard-field rationale supports interpreting the additive gradient perturbation as the intended manifold proximal inner-solve error model, so the framework-level claim needs a source.

children.title: Geometry Failure Boundary
children.top_down_role: Retraction, transport, distance, or tangent-model mismatches that invalidate local behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Geometry Failure Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A non-retraction update can destroy manifold feasibility and intrinsic convergence claims.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On the unit sphere \(\mathbb S^{n-1}\), let \(x\in\mathbb S^{n-1}\) and choose a nonzero tangent vector \(\eta\in T_x\mathbb S^{n-1}\). Replacing a retraction by ambient addition gives \[\lVert x+\eta\rVert^2=\lVert x\rVert^2+2\langle x,\eta\rangle+\lVert\eta\rVert^2=1+\lVert\eta\rVert^2>1.\] Hence \(x+\eta\notin\mathbb S^{n-1}\). Without a feasibility-preserving retraction or projection, the next intrinsic gradient, tangent proximal model, and manifold stationarity measure need not even be defined.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Ambient addition leaves the sphere after every nonzero tangent step, so manifold proximal-gradient guarantees fail without a valid geometric update.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x+\eta\notin\mathbb S^{n-1}\), and an intrinsic next iteration is undefined without geometric correction.
review_flags: The computation is elementary, but the supplied sources do not document this manifold failure boundary.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits and the sphere calculation is correct. The record nevertheless has no cited evidence or standard-field rationale connecting this elementary feasibility failure to the exact manifold proximal-gradient container.

children.title: Coupled Error Amplification
children.top_down_role: Regimes where geometric distortion magnifies proximal-subproblem error.

knowledge_statements.title: Coupled Error Amplification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interaction of geometric distortion and inexact proximal residuals near instability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the exact local error recursion is contractive with factor \(q<1\), while retraction or transport distortion contributes \(a_kd_k\) and the inexact inner solve contributes \(b_k\), giving \[d_{k+1}\leq(q+a_k)d_k+b_k.\] If \(q+a_k\leq\bar q<1\), then errors are damped and \(d_k\leq\bar q^kd_0+\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}\bar q^{k-1-j}b_j\). If instead \(q+a_k\geq1\) persistently, even bounded nonzero \(b_k\) can accumulate rather than decay; no convergence conclusion follows from the exact-method contraction alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Geometry error weakens contraction while inner error supplies forcing; once their combined factor reaches one, persistent errors may accumulate.
assumptions_latex: The displayed perturbed one-step recursion holds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Uniform robustness requires both \(\sup_k(q+a_k)<1\) and forcing errors \(b_k\) compatible with the desired limiting accuracy.

notation.meaning: distance or local error at iteration k

review_flags: This abstract perturbation boundary needs a source connecting the recursion to manifold proximal-gradient methods.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The perturbation inequality and its convolution bound under a uniform contraction are correct, but the conclusion overstates \(\sup_k(q+a_k)<1\) as necessary: nonuniform factors with supremum one can still have decaying products. No source connects the abstract recursion to the intended manifold proximal-gradient error mechanisms.

children.title: Robustness Threshold Regimes
children.top_down_role: Accuracy plus geometry ranges compatible with stable convergence behavior.

assumptions_latex: \(h:\mathcal M\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) is proper and the inexact proximal step is well-defined.
The computed step differs from an exact proximal step by a tangent error \(e_k\) with \(\lVert e_k\rVert\leq\varepsilon_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_k\varepsilon_k<\infty\) is a standard robustness regime; without comparable cumulative-error control, convergence cannot be guaranteed.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive-error boundary for inexact manifold proximal iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider an inexact proximal iteration whose computed tangent step has additive error \(e_k\), with \(\lVert e_k\rVert\leq\varepsilon_k\). A summable-error regime \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\varepsilon_k<\infty\) prevents unbounded accumulation in standard descent arguments. If this control is removed, convergence is not guaranteed even on the flat manifold \(\mathcal M=\mathbb R\): for the zero objective, the admissible iteration \(x_{k+1}=x_k+e_k\) with \(e_k=1/(k+1)\) has vanishing errors but \(x_k\to+\infty\). Thus pointwise decay \(\varepsilon_k\to0\) alone is below the robustness threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Summable proximal errors are controllable, whereas merely vanishing errors may accumulate and cause divergence even on the real line.
knowledge_statements.title: Robustness Threshold Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits, and the flat-manifold example is mathematically plausible, but summability is presented as a sufficient robustness threshold without specifying the proximal iteration and descent hypotheses under which it suffices. A manifold-specific convergence source is required.

assumptions_latex: \((\mathcal M,g)\) is a Riemannian manifold equipped with a retraction \(R\).
\(f:\mathcal M\to\mathbb R\) is locally Lipschitz and a subgradient oracle returns \(v_k\in\partial f(x_k)\subseteq T_{x_k}\mathcal M\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The update is \(x_{k+1}=R_{x_k}(-\alpha_k v_k)\), terminating when \(\lVert v_k\rVert\) satisfies a prescribed stationarity tolerance.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Basic retraction-based nonsmooth descent interface.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x_0\in\mathcal M\), for \(k=0,1,\ldots\), query a Riemannian subgradient \(v_k\in\partial f(x_k)\). If \(\lVert v_k\rVert_{x_k}\leq\epsilon\), return \(x_k\). Otherwise choose \(\alpha_k>0\) and set \[x_{k+1}=R_{x_k}(-\alpha_k v_k).\] If no finite stopping time occurs, the output is the generated sequence. Convergence assertions require additional hypotheses, typically geodesic convexity or weak convexity, bounded subgradients, and a step-size rule such as \(\sum_k\alpha_k=\infty\) and \(\sum_k\alpha_k^2<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each iterate, retract a negative Riemannian subgradient step and stop when the selected subgradient norm is small.
knowledge_statements.title: Riemannian Subgradient Methods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the method container, but the chosen intrinsic subdifferential is not defined and the significance of testing one oracle-selected subgradient requires qualification. An authoritative Riemannian nonsmooth-method source is needed.

children.title: Gradient-Sampling Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Geometric interfaces for sample-based treatment of nonsmooth manifold objectives.

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathcal M\to\mathbb R\) is locally Lipschitz and differentiable almost everywhere near \(x\).
A retraction and vector transport \(\mathcal T_{y\to x}:T_y\mathcal M\to T_x\mathcal M\) are available locally.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The minimum-norm vector in the convex hull of transported sampled gradients supplies an approximate generalized-gradient direction at \(x\).

notation.meaning: transport from the sampled tangent space to the base tangent space
sampled convex hull in the base tangent space

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transported finite-sample approximation of a generalized gradient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At \(x\in\mathcal M\), sample differentiability points \(y_1,\ldots,y_m\) in a retraction ball of radius \(r\), and form \[G_{m,r}(x)=\operatorname{conv}\bigl\{\mathcal T_{y_i\to x}\operatorname{grad}f(y_i):1\leq i\leq m\bigr\}\subseteq T_x\mathcal M.\] Compute \(g_{m,r}(x)\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{g\in G_{m,r}(x)}\lVert g\rVert_x\). If \(\lVert g_{m,r}(x)\rVert_x\leq\epsilon\), return \(x\); otherwise choose \(\alpha>0\) by an acceptance rule and update \(x^+=R_x(-\alpha g_{m,r}(x))\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sample nearby gradients, transport them to one tangent space, and descend along the minimum-norm vector in their convex hull.
knowledge_statements.title: Gradient-Sampling Interfaces

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm matches the interface title, but no source supports the sampling rule, transport requirements, acceptance rule, or interpretation of the finite convex hull as an approximate generalized gradient.

children.title: Smoothing Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Smooth surrogate interfaces for nonsmooth manifold objectives.

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathcal M\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) admits smooth approximants \(f_\mu\) for \(\mu>0\).
On the region of interest, \(\lvert f_\mu(x)-f(x)\rvert\leq b(\mu)\) with \(b(\mu)\to0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A smoothing interface replaces nonsmooth stationarity by smooth stationarity while explicitly retaining the approximation bias \(b(\mu)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract bias-controlled smoothing on a manifold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A smoothing interface for \(f\) is a family \(\{f_\mu\}_{\mu>0}\) such that each \(f_\mu:\mathcal M\to\mathbb R\) is continuously differentiable and \[\sup_{x\in D}\lvert f_\mu(x)-f(x)\rvert\leq b(\mu),\qquad b(\mu)\to0,\] on a specified domain \(D\subseteq\mathcal M\). An algorithm may compute \(x_\mu\) satisfying \(\lVert\operatorname{grad}f_\mu(x_\mu)\rVert\leq\eta\), but the resulting certificate must report both \(\eta\) and \(b(\mu)\); smooth stationarity alone is not an exact stationarity certificate for \(f\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A smoothing interface optimizes a differentiable approximation while tracking both its gradient residual and its bias from the original objective.
knowledge_statements.title: Smoothing Interfaces

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits, but the uniform finite bias bound must be restricted to points where the extended-valued objective is finite. Moreover, function-value bias alone does not provide a stationarity transfer from the smoothed objective to the original objective.

children.title: Sampling–Smoothing Regime Selection
children.top_down_role: Problem regimes governing the choice between sampled gradients, smooth surrogates, or hybrid treatments.

assumptions_latex: Gradient sampling at radius \(r\) has estimation error \(s(m,r,\delta)\) with probability at least \(1-\delta\).
Smoothing with parameter \(\mu\) has bias \(b(\mu)\) and smooth-solver residual \(\eta\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Select an interface whose total certified error meets the target tolerance and whose oracle cost is smallest among admissible parameter choices.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Error-budget rule for choosing a nonsmooth approximation interface.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For target tolerance \(\epsilon>0\) and failure probability \(\delta\), a sampling regime \((m,r)\) is admissible when its certified stationarity error satisfies \(s(m,r,\delta)\leq\epsilon\). A smoothing regime \((\mu,\eta)\) is admissible when an established transfer bound gives \(b(\mu)+\eta\leq\epsilon\). Among admissible regimes, select the one minimizing the relevant cost, such as function evaluations, gradient evaluations, or transports. This is a selection principle only after \(s\) and the smoothing transfer bound have been proved for the chosen geometry and generalized derivative.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose sampling or smoothing by meeting a common stationarity-error budget, then minimize the relevant oracle and transport cost.
knowledge_statements.title: Sampling–Smoothing Regime Selection

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The selection-principle kind fits, but the asserted comparison depends on unprovided stationarity-transfer theorems. A function-value smoothing bias cannot generally be added directly to a gradient residual without further assumptions and compatible scaling.

children.title: Curvature-Sensitive Interface Failures
children.top_down_role: Breakdown modes caused by geometric distortion of sampling neighborhoods or smoothing surrogates.

assumptions_latex: Sampled gradients lie in distinct tangent spaces \(T_y\mathcal M\).
The implementation combines these gradients without a valid transport into one base tangent space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The resulting combination need not be a tangent descent direction or approximate any intrinsic generalized gradient.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure caused by combining vectors from incompatible tangent spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(\mathcal M=\mathbb S^{n-1}\), tangent vectors satisfy \(T_y\mathcal M=\{v:\langle v,y\rangle=0\}\). For distinct samples \(y_i\), the vectors \(g_i=\operatorname{grad}f(y_i)\) belong to different spaces \(T_{y_i}\mathcal M\). Their ambient average \(\bar g=m^{-1}\sum_i g_i\) generally satisfies \(\langle\bar g,x\rangle\neq0\) at the base point \(x\), so \(R_x(-\alpha\bar g)\) is not even defined for a retraction whose input domain is \(T_x\mathcal M\). Valid transport or projection, with controlled distortion, is therefore necessary for an intrinsic sampling or smoothing interface.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without transport, sampled manifold gradients cannot be intrinsically averaged and may fail even to define a valid retraction step.
knowledge_statements.title: Curvature-Sensitive Interface Failures

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits, and the sphere calculation correctly exposes incompatible tangent spaces. However, the conclusion overextends the argument to smoothing interfaces generally, and the need for transport with controlled distortion requires a geometry-specific source.

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathcal M\to\mathbb R\) admits local cutting models transported to a common tangent space.
A retraction, vector transport, and positive stabilization parameter are available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The bundle subproblem produces a stabilized trial direction, and acceptance compares actual decrease with model-predicted decrease.

notation.meaning: bundle cutting model in the current tangent space

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Retraction-based stabilized bundle interface with serious and null steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(x_0\in\mathcal M\) and a bundle of function values and subgradients. At iteration \(k\), transport retained cuts into \(T_{x_k}\mathcal M\) and form a model \(m_k:T_{x_k}\mathcal M\to\mathbb R\). Compute \[\eta_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\eta\in T_{x_k}\mathcal M}\left\{m_k(\eta)+\frac{1}{2\lambda_k}\lVert\eta\rVert_{x_k}^2\right\}.\] Evaluate \(y_k=R_{x_k}(\eta_k)\). Accept \(x_{k+1}=y_k\) when actual decrease is a prescribed fraction of predicted decrease; otherwise set \(x_{k+1}=x_k\), add the new cut, and update \(\lambda_k\). Stop when the model residual meets tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A manifold bundle method minimizes a stabilized transported cutting model and uses serious or null steps according to actual model agreement.
knowledge_statements.title: Manifold Bundle-Method Interfaces

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits, but the cutting model, predicted-decrease quantity, cut transport, stabilization update, and model residual are not defined sufficiently to identify a valid manifold bundle method. A specific algorithmic source is required.

assumptions_latex: \(D\subseteq\mathcal M\) is geodesically convex and any \(x,y\in D\) are joined by a selected minimizing geodesic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every intrinsic subgradient satisfies a curvature-compatible quadratic support inequality along the selected geodesic.

notation.meaning: Riemannian logarithm at x along the selected minimizing geodesic
intrinsic subgradient of f at x

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic support form of geodesic weak convexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(x,y\in D\) and every compatible intrinsic subgradient \(v\in\partial f(x)\), geodesic \(\rho\)-weak convexity yields \[f(y)\geq f(x)+\langle v,\log_x(y)\rangle_x-\frac{\rho}{2}d(x,y)^2.\] The quadratic term records the permitted nonsmooth nonconvexity relative to the manifold distance. Any use of this inequality must remain inside a region where the selected logarithm is single-valued and where the adopted generalized subdifferential supports the displayed inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Geodesic weak convexity gives subgradients a quadratic support inequality, valid only where the logarithm and generalized derivative are compatible.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonsmoothness–Curvature Interaction

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property kind fits the interaction container, but the displayed global support inequality is convention-dependent and need not follow for every generalized subgradient from an unspecified definition of geodesic weak convexity. A source fixing the curvature, logarithm, and subdifferential conventions is required.

assumptions_latex: \(F(x)=\mathbb E_\xi[f(x;\xi)]+h(x)\), with stochastic tangent gradients available for the smooth term.
A retraction \(R\) is available and the tangent proximal subproblem has a minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each iteration solves a tangent stochastic proximal model and retracts its minimizer to the manifold.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tangent-model stochastic proximal-gradient iteration.

source_refs.locator: 7.1 Stochastic forward-backward method p. 162
source_refs.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose \(x_0\in\mathcal M\). At iteration \(k\), sample \(\xi_k\) and form an unbiased or controlled-bias estimator \(g_k\in T_{x_k}\mathcal M\) of \(\operatorname{grad}\mathbb E[f(x_k;\xi)]\). Compute \[\eta_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\eta\in T_{x_k}\mathcal M}\left\{\langle g_k,\eta\rangle_{x_k}+\frac{1}{2\alpha_k}\lVert\eta\rVert_{x_k}^2+h(R_{x_k}(\eta))\right\},\] and set \(x_{k+1}=R_{x_k}(\eta_k)\). Stop when a prescribed proximal-gradient residual or iteration budget is reached; otherwise output a specified sampled iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Estimate the smooth gradient stochastically, solve a proximal model in the current tangent space, and retract the resulting step.
knowledge_statements.title: Riemannian Stochastic Proximal Gradient

source_witnesses.locator: 7.1 Stochastic forward-backward method p. 162
source_witnesses.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits, but the cited section covers Euclidean stochastic forward-backward splitting rather than the stated retraction-based manifold proximal model. A manifold-specific source must support the subproblem, estimator conditions, residual, and output rule.

assumptions_latex: \(F(x)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x)+h(x)\), with component Riemannian gradients available.
A vector transport compares component gradients computed at different iterates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A control-variate estimator replaces the raw stochastic gradient in the tangent proximal update.

notation.meaning: transport from the reference tangent space

knowledge_statements.scope_note: SVRG-type control variate inside a manifold proximal step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a reference point \(\widetilde x\), compute \(\widetilde g=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\operatorname{grad}f_i(\widetilde x)\). For a sampled index \(i_k\), form \[v_k=\operatorname{grad}f_{i_k}(x_k)-\mathcal T_{\widetilde x\to x_k}\operatorname{grad}f_{i_k}(\widetilde x)+\mathcal T_{\widetilde x\to x_k}\widetilde g.\] Replace the stochastic gradient by \(v_k\) in the tangent proximal subproblem, compute its minimizer \(\eta_k\), and set \(x_{k+1}=R_{x_k}(\eta_k)\). Periodically refresh \(\widetilde x\) and \(\widetilde g\); stop using the chosen proximal-stationarity criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use transported component-gradient differences around a periodically refreshed reference point to reduce variance in manifold proximal updates.
knowledge_statements.title: Variance-Reduced Proximal Methods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits, but the SVRG-type estimator and proximal extension require a source specifying index sampling, transport properties, refresh schedule, and any bias introduced by non-isometric or nonlinear transport.

assumptions_latex: An online stochastic first-order oracle returns unbiased tangent gradients with bounded variance.
The smooth expectation has a retraction-compatible Lipschitz gradient and the composite proximal model is solvable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A standard minibatch stochastic proximal-gradient regime targets \(\mathbb E[\lVert G_\alpha(x_R)\rVert^2]\leq\epsilon^2\) using order \(\epsilon^{-4}\) stochastic gradients and \(\epsilon^{-2}\) proximal steps.

notation.meaning: manifold proximal-gradient mapping associated with the tangent model

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Baseline nonconvex online first-order complexity, pending manifold-specific certification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In the online oracle model, count each sampled stochastic gradient as one oracle call and each solved tangent proximal subproblem as one proximal call. Under bounded variance and retraction-smoothness assumptions, the baseline minibatch regime is expected to return a random iterate \(x_R\) satisfying \[\mathbb E\bigl[\lVert G_\alpha(x_R)\rVert^2\bigr]\leq\epsilon^2\] after \(O(\epsilon^{-4})\) stochastic-gradient oracle calls and \(O(\epsilon^{-2})\) proximal calls. The constants depend on initial objective gap, smoothness, variance, and geometric regularity; the precise bound requires a fixed proximal-gradient mapping and retraction model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Baseline online stochastic proximal gradient typically needs order epsilon-to-the-minus-four sampled gradients for expected epsilon-stationarity.
knowledge_statements.title: Online Composite Oracle Complexity

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound kind is correct, but the claimed oracle orders are theorem-level assertions and are explicitly presented only as expected baseline behavior. A manifold-specific theorem fixing the proximal-gradient mapping, batch schedule, geometric assumptions, and counting model is required.

assumptions_latex: \(F(x)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x)+h(x)\) and component-gradient calls are counted separately.
A variance-reduced manifold proximal method satisfies the required transport, smoothness, and bounded-level-set conditions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A representative target is \(O(n+\sqrt n\,\epsilon^{-2})\) component-gradient calls for \(\mathbb E[\lVert G_\alpha(x_R)\rVert^2]\leq\epsilon^2\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representative finite-sum variance-reduced complexity target.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In the incremental first-order oracle model, one evaluation of \(\operatorname{grad}f_i(x)\) costs one component-gradient call, while tangent proximal solves are counted separately. For suitable variance-reduced proximal schemes, a representative finite-sum target is to produce \(x_R\) satisfying \[\mathbb E\bigl[\lVert G_\alpha(x_R)\rVert^2\bigr]\leq\epsilon^2\] using \(O(n+\sqrt n\,\epsilon^{-2})\) component-gradient calls. This rate is not universal: refresh schedules, transport accuracy, retraction order, component smoothness, and the definition of \(G_\alpha\) must be fixed before the bound can be certified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A representative variance-reduced finite-sum target is n plus square-root-n times epsilon-to-the-minus-two component-gradient calls.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Sum Composite Oracle Complexity

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound kind fits, but the rate is described as merely representative and varies with the variance-reduction scheme and geometric conventions. It cannot be retained as a mathematical bound without an exact manifold finite-sum theorem and locator.

assumptions_latex: \(M\) is a smooth Riemannian manifold and \(f:M\to\mathbb R\), \(c:M\to\mathbb R^m\) are continuously differentiable.
\(\rho>0\), and each primal subproblem admits an acceptable approximate solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^{k+1}\approx\arg\min_{x\in M}\mathcal L_{\rho_k}(x,\lambda^k)\), followed by \(\lambda^{k+1}=\lambda^k+\rho_k c(x^{k+1})\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality-constrained Riemannian augmented-Lagrangian interface with Euclidean multipliers.

source_refs.source_title: Parallel and Distributed Computation: Numerical Methods

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the problem \(\min_{x\in M} f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\), define the manifold augmented Lagrangian by \[\mathcal L_\rho(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\langle\lambda,c(x)\rangle+\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert c(x)\rVert^2.\] At iteration \(k\), approximately minimize \(\mathcal L_{\rho_k}(\cdot,\lambda^k)\) over \(M\), using Riemannian derivatives and a retraction, and then set \(\lambda^{k+1}=\lambda^k+\rho_kc(x^{k+1})\). A stopping interface reports primal residual \(\lVert c(x^{k+1})\rVert\) and Riemannian stationarity residual \(\lVert\operatorname{grad}_x\mathcal L_{\rho_k}(x^{k+1},\lambda^{k+1})\rVert\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The interface alternates manifold-constrained minimization of an augmented Lagrangian with a Euclidean multiplier update and reports feasibility and Riemannian stationarity residuals.
knowledge_statements.title: Manifold Augmented-Lagrangian Interface

children.title: Manifold ADMM Formulations
children.top_down_role: ADMM-style formulations whose variable blocks include manifold-constrained components.

assumptions_latex: \(M\) is a smooth manifold embedded in a finite-dimensional Hilbert space \(E\).
\(f:M\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), \(g:E\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), and \(A:M\to E\) define well-posed block subproblems.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The iterates alternately minimize the scaled augmented objective over \(M\) and \(E\), then update the scaled dual residual.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scaled two-block ADMM syntax; no general convergence claim is included.

source_refs.locator: 2.7 Operator splitting p. 45
source_refs.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min_{x\in M,\ z\in E} f(x)+g(z)\) subject to \(A(x)-z=0\), initialize \(z^0,u^0\in E\). For \(k=0,1,\ldots\), compute \[x^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in M}\left(f(x)+\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert A(x)-z^k+u^k\rVert^2\right),\] \[z^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{z\in E}\left(g(z)+\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert A(x^{k+1})-z+u^k\rVert^2\right),\] and \(u^{k+1}=u^k+A(x^{k+1})-z^{k+1}\). Stop when prescribed primal and dual residual tolerances hold; otherwise return the latest primal blocks and residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Manifold ADMM updates a manifold block, an auxiliary ambient block, and a scaled dual variable for a split equality constraint.
knowledge_statements.title: Manifold ADMM Formulations

children.title: Operator-Splitting Formulations
children.top_down_role: Operator decompositions adapted to geometric domains or tangent-space representations.

assumptions_latex: \(M\) is a closed embedded submanifold of a finite-dimensional Hilbert space \(E\).
\(f:E\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) and \(g:E\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) are proper functions with defined limiting subdifferentials.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Constrained stationarity is represented by \(0\in\partial f(x)+\partial g(x)+N_M(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ambient inclusion representation for an embedded, generally nonconvex manifold.

source_refs.locator: 1.2 Limitations of monotone operator theory p. 2

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Extend the constrained objective as \(F=f+g+\delta_M\) on \(E\), where \(\delta_M(x)=0\) for \(x\in M\) and \(\delta_M(x)=+\infty\) otherwise. At \(x\in M\), first-order stationarity is represented by \[0\in\partial f(x)+\partial g(x)+N_M(x).\] Thus one may assign terms to set-valued blocks, for example \(A=\partial f+N_M\) and \(B=\partial g\), and write \(0\in A(x)+B(x)\). If \(M\) is nonconvex, these blocks need not be monotone, so classical monotone-splitting convergence does not follow from this representation alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An embedded manifold constraint can be encoded by its indicator and normal cone, producing a split stationarity inclusion without implying monotone-operator convergence.

children.title: Geometry-Compatible Variable Blocks
children.top_down_role: Block structures for which splitting operations remain compatible with manifold representations.

assumptions_latex: Each \(M_i\) is a smooth Riemannian manifold with metric \(g_i\) and retraction \(R^{(i)}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The blocks are geometry-compatible when their tangent, metric, and retraction operations form the corresponding product structures.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility predicate for block algorithms on product manifolds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A variable blocking \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_q)\in M\) is geometry-compatible when \[T_xM=T_{x_1}M_1\times\cdots\times T_{x_q}M_q,\qquad g_x(\eta,\zeta)=\sum_{i=1}^q g_{i,x_i}(\eta_i,\zeta_i),\] and its block update uses the product retraction \[R_x(\eta)=\bigl(R^{(1)}_{x_1}(\eta_1),\ldots,R^{(q)}_{x_q}(\eta_q)\bigr).\] Any coupling residual compared across distinct tangent spaces must additionally be transported or represented in a common ambient space. Under these conditions, a block direction and its update remain well typed in the product geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Variable blocks are compatible when tangent spaces, metrics, and retractions have matching product structure, with cross-block residuals compared in a common space.
knowledge_statements.title: Geometry-Compatible Variable Blocks

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits the compatibility leaf, and the product tangent, metric, and retraction formulas are coherent. No source is supplied for these geometric claims or for the cross-tangent-space residual requirement.

assumptions_latex: \(h:M\to\mathbb R^p\) and \(g:M\to\mathbb R^q\) are continuously differentiable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The additional constraints define \(F=\{x\in M:h(x)=0,\ g(x)\leq0\}\) and the displayed linearized cone at each feasible point.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The feasible set for additional smooth manifold constraints is \[F=\{x\in M:h(x)=0,\ g_j(x)\leq0\text{ for }j=1,\ldots,q\}.\] For \(x\in F\), define \(I(x)=\{j:g_j(x)=0\}\). The associated linearized feasible cone is \[\mathcal L_F(x)=\{\eta\in T_xM:D h(x)[\eta]=0,\ D g_j(x)[\eta]\leq0\text{ for every }j\in I(x)\}.\] Thus an implementation must expose function values and tangent-linear derivative actions for \(h\) and \(g\), while preserving the base requirement that trial points and retracted updates lie on \(M\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Additional equalities and inequalities restrict the manifold feasible set; their derivatives define a tangent-space linearized feasibility cone at each feasible point.

assumptions_latex: \(M\) is an embedded submanifold of a Euclidean space \(E\) with the induced metric.
\(f:M\to\mathbb R\) has a differentiable ambient extension \(\bar f\) near \(M\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{grad}f(x)=P_x\nabla\bar f(x)\), independently of the chosen extension.

notation.meaning: orthogonal projection onto the tangent space

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Induced-metric conversion for embedded manifolds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(x\in M\), let \(P_x:E\to T_xM\) be the orthogonal projector. The Riemannian gradient is obtained from any smooth ambient extension by \[\operatorname{grad}f(x)=P_x\nabla\bar f(x).\] Indeed, its defining identity is \[\langle\operatorname{grad}f(x),\eta\rangle= D\bar f(x)[\eta]\qquad\text{for every }\eta\in T_xM.\] Although \(\nabla\bar f(x)\) may depend on the extension away from \(M\), its tangent projection does not. For a non-induced metric, the conversion must instead apply the metric-dependent Riesz map and cannot be replaced by orthogonal projection alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On an embedded manifold with induced metric, project any ambient extension's Euclidean gradient onto the tangent space to obtain the Riemannian gradient.
knowledge_statements.title: Ambient-to-Riemannian Derivative Conversion

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind exactly fits ambient-to-Riemannian conversion, and the induced-metric projection formula is precise. No source is supplied for extension independence or the non-induced-metric boundary.

assumptions_latex: \(M\) is an embedded Riemannian submanifold of a Euclidean space \(E\) with induced metric.
\(f:M\to\mathbb R\) has a twice differentiable ambient extension \(\bar f\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Hess}f(x)[\eta]=P_xD(P_{(\cdot)}\nabla\bar f(\cdot))(x)[\eta]\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Matrix-free Hessian action for an induced embedded geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(x\in M\) and \(\eta\in T_xM\), the Riemannian Hessian-vector product is the covariant derivative \[\operatorname{Hess}f(x)[\eta]=
abla^{M}_{\eta}\operatorname{grad}f.\] In the induced embedded geometry it can be evaluated without forming a Hessian matrix as \[\operatorname{Hess}f(x)[\eta]=P_xD igl(P_{(\cdot)}
abla ar f(\cdot) igr)(x)[\eta].\] Expanding the derivative yields \(P_x
abla^2 ar f(x)[\eta]+P_x(DP_x[\eta])
abla ar f(x)\); the second term accounts for variation of the tangent space. The returned vector lies in \(T_xM\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Riemannian Hessian-vector product differentiates the projected gradient and includes both the ambient Hessian action and tangent-space curvature correction.
knowledge_statements.title: Riemannian Hessian–Vector Products

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits the Hessian-vector-product leaf, and the projected derivative formula includes the required tangent-space variation term. No source is supplied for the embedded-manifold Hessian identity.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Transporter-corrected representation of a Riemannian Hessian–vector product
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An exact limit formula using transported gradient differences and a correction for variation of the transporter-induced frame.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let c be a smooth curve on \mathcal M with c(0)=x and c'(0)=u. For any transporter \mathrm T, any orthonormal basis v_1,\ldots,v_d of T_x\mathcal M, and V_i(t)=(\mathrm T_{x\leftarrow c(t)})^{-1}(v_i),
\[
\operatorname{Hess}f(x)[u]=\lim_{t\to0}\frac{\mathrm T_{x\leftarrow c(t)}\operatorname{grad}f(c(t))-\operatorname{grad}f(x)}{t}+\sum_{i=1}^d\langle\operatorname{grad}f(x),v_i\rangle_x\frac{\mathrm D}{\mathrm dt}V_i(0).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Riemannian Hessian applied to the initial velocity of a smooth curve equals the limit of transported gradient differences plus a correction for variation of the frame induced by the chosen transporter.
assumptions_latex: c\text{ is a smooth curve on the Riemannian manifold }\mathcal M
(v_1,\ldots,v_d)\text{ is an orthonormal basis of }T_x\mathcal M
\operatorname{grad}f\text{ and }\operatorname{Hess}f\text{ are defined at the indicated points and direction}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{Hess}f(x)[u]=\lim_{t\to0}\frac{\mathrm T_{x\leftarrow c(t)}\operatorname{grad}f(c(t))-\operatorname{grad}f(x)}{t}+\sum_{i=1}^d\langle\operatorname{grad}f(x),v_i\rangle_x\frac{\mathrm D}{\mathrm dt}V_i(0)

assumptions_latex: \(M\) is an embedded manifold with induced metric and a differentiable tangent projector \(P_x\).
\(f\) is represented by a differentiable ambient computational graph for an extension \(\bar f\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Automatic differentiation supplies ambient derivative actions, while projection and differentiated projection convert them into Riemannian derivatives.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Embedded-manifold differentiation pipeline, not a claim about every AD representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Automatic differentiation may evaluate the ambient quantities \(
abla ar f(x)\) and \(
abla^2 ar f(x)[\eta]\), but the manifold interface must perform the geometric conversion. For first order, return \[\operatorname{grad}f(x)=P_x
abla ar f(x).\] For second order, differentiate the complete projected-gradient program and project its output: \[\operatorname{Hess}f(x)[\eta]=P_xD igl(P_{(\cdot)}
abla ar f(\cdot) igr)(x)[\eta].\] Consequently, differentiating only the ambient objective omits the derivative of \(P_x\) and generally gives an incorrect Riemannian Hessian action on curved manifolds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Automatic differentiation computes ambient derivatives; correct manifold gradients and Hessian actions additionally require tangent projection and differentiation of that projection.
knowledge_statements.title: Automatic Differentiation on Manifolds

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle kind fits the automatic-differentiation leaf, and the statement correctly separates ambient AD from geometric conversion for the stated embedded induced-metric setting. No source supports the first- and second-order pipeline or its failure warning.

children.title: Riemannian Gradient Consistency Checks
children.top_down_role: Diagnostics for agreement between implemented gradients, manifold metrics, and directional behavior.

assumptions_latex: \(f:M\to\mathbb R\) is three times continuously differentiable near \(x\).
\(R_x\) is a smooth retraction and \(\eta\in T_xM\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A correct gradient satisfies \(\delta_g(t,\eta)=O(t^2)\) as \(t\to0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Central retraction finite-difference check for a supplied gradient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a candidate gradient \(g_x\in T_xM\), a directional consistency residual at nonzero step \(t\) is \[\delta_g(t,\eta)=\frac{f(R_x(t\eta))-f(R_x(-t\eta))}{2t}-\langle g_x,\eta\rangle_x.\] Because \(D R_x(0)\) is the identity on \(T_xM\), correctness of \(g_x=\operatorname{grad}f(x)\) implies \(\delta_g(t,\eta)=O(t^2)\) as \(t\to0\). A numerical check samples nonzero tangent directions and verifies the predicted decay over a range of steps before roundoff dominates; one isolated small residual is not a consistency test.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compare gradient directional products with centered function differences along a retraction; a correct gradient exhibits second-order residual decay before roundoff dominates.
knowledge_statements.title: Riemannian Gradient Consistency Checks

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits a consistency-check leaf, and the centered retraction test is coherently stated under the given smoothness. No source is supplied for the second-order residual-decay criterion or numerical validation guidance.

children.title: Riemannian Hessian Consistency Checks
children.top_down_role: Diagnostics for implemented Hessian actions, symmetry behavior, and geometric second-order structure.

assumptions_latex: \(f:M\to\mathbb R\) is sufficiently smooth and \(H_x:T_xM\to T_xM\) is a candidate Hessian action.
\(R_x\) is a smooth retraction and \(\mathcal P_{t\to0}\) is parallel transport along \(t\mapsto R_x(t\eta)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A correct Hessian is self-adjoint and satisfies \(\delta_H(t,\eta)=O(t^2)\) under the stated smoothness.

notation.meaning: parallel transport back to the base tangent space

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transported finite-difference and symmetry checks for a Hessian action.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\eta\in T_xM\) and nonzero \(t\), define \[\delta_H(t,\eta)=\frac{\mathcal P_{t\to0}\operatorname{grad}f(R_x(t\eta))-\mathcal P_{-t\to0}\operatorname{grad}f(R_x(-t\eta))}{2t}-H_x[\eta].\] A consistent Riemannian Hessian action satisfies \(\lVert\delta_H(t,\eta)\rVert_x=O(t^2)\) under adequate smoothness. It must also satisfy the self-adjointness check \[\langle\zeta,H_x[\eta]\rangle_x=\langle H_x[\zeta],\eta\rangle_x\qquad\text{for all }\eta,\zeta\in T_xM.\] Numerical validation tests decay and symmetry for several tangent directions before cancellation and roundoff dominate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Validate Hessian actions by centered differences of transported gradients and by metric self-adjointness, checking convergence across several step sizes and tangent directions.
knowledge_statements.title: Riemannian Hessian Consistency Checks

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits, but “sufficiently smooth” and “adequate smoothness” do not specify assumptions sufficient for the claimed second-order centered-difference error, and the required regularity of the retraction curve and parallel transport is unstated. No supporting source is supplied.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Numerical consistency check for a Riemannian Hessian implementation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diagnostic combining tangent-space, linearity, self-adjointness, and pullback Taylor-residual checks. Cubic residual decay is guaranteed under an exact second-order-retraction or critical-point condition; using only an approximate critical point makes the test less conclusive.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: First check numerically that \operatorname{Hess}f(x)[u]\in T_x\mathcal M, that \operatorname{Hess}f(x)[au+bv]=a\operatorname{Hess}f(x)[u]+b\operatorname{Hess}f(x)[v], and that \langle u,\operatorname{Hess}f(x)[v]\rangle_x=\langle\operatorname{Hess}f(x)[u],v\rangle_x, up to machine precision. After checking the gradient implementation, choose \|v\|_x=1 and define E(t)=\left|f(R_x(tv))-f(x)-t\langle\operatorname{grad}f(x),v\rangle_x-\frac{t^2}{2}\langle\operatorname{Hess}f(x)[v],v\rangle_x\right|. If R is a second-order retraction or \operatorname{grad}f(x)=0, evaluate E(t) at logarithmically spaced values of t and look for a log-log slope of at least three over one or two orders of magnitude.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Validate that the implemented Riemannian Hessian is tangent-valued, linear, and self-adjoint to machine precision. After validating the gradient, subtract the quadratic Taylor model along a unit tangent direction and plot the residual against the step size on logarithmic axes. With a second-order retraction at an arbitrary point, or at an exact critical point with another retraction, the residual should decay cubically or faster for sufficiently small steps. The slope need only appear over part of the tested range, and a test conducted at merely an approximate critical point is less conclusive.
assumptions_latex: f:\mathcal M\to\mathbb R\text{ is smooth on the Riemannian manifold }\mathcal M
R\text{ is a second-order retraction, or }\operatorname{grad}f(x)=0
\text{The Riemannian gradient implementation has already been checked}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: E(t)=O(t^3)\text{ under the stated exact condition; hence a correct implementation should exhibit asymptotic log-log slope at least }3\text{ over a suitable small-}t\text{ range.}

children.title: Cross-Order Derivative Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Consistency relationships between first-order and second-order derivative implementations.

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Order Derivative Diagnostics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint directional validation of candidate Riemannian gradients and Hessians through Taylor residual orders.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(\rho_1(t)=f(R_x(t\eta))-f(x)-t\langle g_x,\eta\rangle_x\) and \(\rho_2(t)=\rho_1(t)-\tfrac12t^2\langle H_x\eta,\eta\rangle_x\). The pair \((g_x,H_x)\) passes the cross-order directional diagnostic along \(\eta\) when \[\limsup_{t\to0}\frac{|\rho_1(t)|}{t^2}<\infty,\qquad \limsup_{t\to0}\frac{|\rho_2(t)|}{|t|^3}<\infty.\] When it passes, \(\rho_1(t)=O(t^2)\) and \(\rho_2(t)=O(|t|^3)\) as \(t\to0\), so the same sampled curve checks the supplied linear and quadratic coefficients in the direction \(\eta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A candidate gradient–Hessian pair passes this directional certificate when the retraction-curve residual is quadratic after subtracting its linear model and cubic after subtracting its quadratic model.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathcal M\to\mathbb R\) is three times continuously differentiable near \(x\).
\(R_x\) is a second-order retraction and \(\eta\in T_x\mathcal M\).
\(g_x\in T_x\mathcal M\) and self-adjoint \(H_x:T_x\mathcal M\to T_x\mathcal M\) are candidate derivatives.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \((g_x,H_x)\) passes the diagnostic along \(\eta\), then \(\rho_1(t)=O(t^2)\) and \(\rho_2(t)=O(|t|^3)\) as \(t\to0\).

notation.meaning: Riemannian metric inner product at x

children.title: Retraction-Based Finite-Difference Validation
children.top_down_role: Numerical derivative checks performed along retraction-generated manifold curves.

knowledge_statements.title: Retraction-Based Finite-Difference Validation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Centered finite-difference validation along a sufficiently smooth second-order retraction curve.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(h\ne0\), compute \[D_1(h)=\frac{f(R_x(h\eta))-f(R_x(-h\eta))}{2h},\qquad D_2(h)=\frac{f(R_x(h\eta))-2f(x)+f(R_x(-h\eta))}{h^2}.\] Then \(D_1(h)=\langle\operatorname{grad}f(x),\eta\rangle_x+O(h^2)\) and \(D_2(h)=\langle\operatorname{Hess}f(x)[\eta],\eta\rangle_x+O(h^2)\) as \(h\to0\). Compare these values with the implemented directional gradient and Hessian quadratic form over a range of nonzero step sizes, allowing for truncation and rounding errors.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compute centered differences along a sufficiently smooth second-order retraction and compare them with implemented gradient and Hessian directional quantities; both differences have second-order truncation error under fourth-order pullback smoothness.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathcal M\to\mathbb R\) and the retraction curve \(t\mapsto R_x(t\eta)\) are sufficiently smooth that \(t\mapsto f(R_x(t\eta))\) is four times continuously differentiable near \(0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D_1(h)=\langle\operatorname{grad}f(x),\eta\rangle_x+O(h^2)\) and \(D_2(h)=\langle\operatorname{Hess}f(x)[\eta],\eta\rangle_x+O(h^2)\) as \(h\to0\).

children.title: Tangent Projection Kernels
children.top_down_role: Kernels mapping ambient quantities into manifold tangent spaces.

assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal M\) is an embedded Riemannian submanifold of an inner-product space \(E\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_xz\in T_x\mathcal M\) and \(z-P_xz\in(T_x\mathcal M)^\perp\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Metric-orthogonal projection onto an embedded manifold's tangent space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \((x,z)\), compute \[P_xz=\underset{\xi\in T_x\mathcal M}{\operatorname{argmin}}\ \|z-\xi\|^2.\] Return \(P_xz\). Equivalently, the kernel is characterized by \(P_x^2=P_x\), \(P_x^*=P_x\), and \(\operatorname{range}(P_x)=T_x\mathcal M\). Hence its output is tangent and its discarded component satisfies \(z-P_xz\in(T_x\mathcal M)^\perp\). A concrete implementation may solve the linearized constraint equations defining \(T_x\mathcal M\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The tangent projection kernel returns the metric-nearest tangent vector and discards a component orthogonal to the tangent space.
knowledge_statements.title: Tangent Projection Kernels

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The orthogonal-projection kernel is mathematically precise and appropriate for the leaf, but it has no citation supporting the embedded-manifold tangent projection characterization.

children.title: Horizontal Projection Kernels
children.top_down_role: Kernels selecting horizontal representatives in quotient-manifold computations.

knowledge_statements.title: Horizontal Projection Kernels
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Orthogonal removal of vertical components in a Riemannian quotient representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(\mathcal V_{\bar x}=\ker D\pi_{\bar x}\) and \(\mathcal H_{\bar x}=\mathcal V_{\bar x}^{\perp}\). Given \(\bar\xi\in T_{\bar x}\overline{\mathcal M}\), compute \(v=\operatorname{argmin}_{w\in\mathcal V_{\bar x}}\|\bar\xi-w\|_{\bar x}^2\), and return \[P^{\mathrm H}_{\bar x}\bar\xi=\bar\xi-v.\] The result lies in \(\mathcal H_{\bar x}\), and removing \(v\) preserves the represented quotient tangent vector because \(D\pi_{\bar x}(v)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The horizontal projection kernel removes the metric-orthogonal vertical component while preserving the tangent vector represented on the quotient manifold.
assumptions_latex: \(\pi:\overline{\mathcal M}\to\mathcal M\) is a Riemannian submersion.
\(\bar x\in\overline{\mathcal M}\) and \(\bar\xi\in T_{\bar x}\overline{\mathcal M}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P^{\mathrm H}_{\bar x}\bar\xi\in\mathcal H_{\bar x}\) and \(D\pi_{\bar x}(P^{\mathrm H}_{\bar x}\bar\xi)=D\pi_{\bar x}(\bar\xi)\).

notation.meaning: vertical space, the kernel of the quotient differential

children.title: Quotient-Lift Projection Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Compatibility between quotient projections, lifted representations, and chosen horizontal spaces.

knowledge_statements.title: Quotient-Lift Projection Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility between horizontal projection and the quotient differential.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(\bar\xi\in T_{\bar x}\overline{\mathcal M}\), vertical removal preserves its pushforward: \[D\pi_{\bar x}(P^{\mathrm H}_{\bar x}\bar\xi)=D\pi_{\bar x}(\bar\xi).\] Since \(D\pi_{\bar x}|_{\mathcal H_{\bar x}}:\mathcal H_{\bar x}\to T_{\pi(\bar x)}\mathcal M\) is an isometric bijection, the projected vector is the unique horizontal lift: \[P^{\mathrm H}_{\bar x}\bar\xi=\operatorname{lift}_{\bar x}(D\pi_{\bar x}\bar\xi).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Horizontal projection preserves the quotient pushforward and produces the unique horizontal lift of the represented quotient tangent vector.
assumptions_latex: \(\pi:\overline{\mathcal M}\to\mathcal M\) is a Riemannian submersion.
\(P^{\mathrm H}_{\bar x}\) is the orthogonal projector onto \(\mathcal H_{\bar x}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D\pi_{\bar x}(P^{\mathrm H}_{\bar x}\bar\xi)=D\pi_{\bar x}(\bar\xi)\) and \(P^{\mathrm H}_{\bar x}\bar\xi=\operatorname{lift}_{\bar x}(D\pi_{\bar x}\bar\xi)\).

children.title: Projection Stability Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Numerical regimes where projection kernels become inaccurate, unstable, or representation-sensitive.

assumptions_latex: \(Y\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\) has full column rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|P(Y)\|_2=1\), but Gram-based evaluation becomes ill-conditioned as \(\sigma_{\min}(Y)\to0\) and loses continuity at rank change.

notation.meaning: orthogonal projector onto the columns of Y

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rank loss is the stability boundary for Gram-inverse projection formulas.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Although the exact orthogonal projector satisfies \(\|P(Y)\|_2=1\), its Gram formula uses \((Y^\top Y)^{-1}\), whose condition number is \(\kappa_2(Y)^2\). Thus numerical sensitivity grows as \(\sigma_{\min}(Y)\to0\). The boundary is sharp: for \(Y_\varepsilon=[e_1,\varepsilon e_2]\) with \(\varepsilon>0\), \(P(Y_\varepsilon)=e_1e_1^\top+e_2e_2^\top\), whereas the pseudoinverse formula at \(\varepsilon=0\) gives \(P(Y_0)=e_1e_1^\top\). Hence the projector is discontinuous when rank changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Orthogonal projectors have unit norm, but Gram-inverse kernels become ill-conditioned near rank loss and the projected subspace can jump at rank change.
knowledge_statements.title: Projection Stability Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The rank-loss example correctly distinguishes the unit norm of the exact nonzero projector from instability of the Gram-inverse evaluation and discontinuity across a rank change. The failure-boundary role fits, but a projection perturbation or numerical linear algebra source is required.

children.title: QR Factorization Kernels
children.top_down_role: QR-based kernels used in manifold representations, projections, or retractions.

assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\) has full column rank with \(n\ge r\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A=QR\), \(Q^\top Q=I_r\), and positive diagonal entries of \(R\) make the thin factorization unique.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Thin QR representation used to construct orthonormal manifold representatives and retractions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A thin QR kernel maps \(A\) to factors \((Q,R)\) satisfying \[A=QR,\qquad Q^\top Q=I_r,\qquad R\in\mathbb R^{r\times r}\text{ upper triangular}.\] If the kernel enforces \(R_{ii}>0\) for every \(i\), then \((Q,R)\) is unique. The factor \(Q\) is therefore a canonical orthonormal representative for full-rank input, while loss of rank prevents the positive-diagonal uniqueness convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Thin QR factors a full-column-rank matrix into an orthonormal factor and a triangular factor; positive triangular diagonal makes the factors unique.
knowledge_statements.title: QR Factorization Kernels

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The thin-QR output contract and positive-diagonal uniqueness statement are correct and fit a factorization-kernel leaf, but no QR source with an inspectable locator is supplied.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Differential of the QR Q-Factor Map
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gives the directional derivative of the specified Q-factor map on full-column-rank matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n,p\in\mathbb{N}\) with \(p\le n\), and let \(\operatorname{qf}:\mathbb{R}_*^{n\times p}\to\operatorname{St}(p,n)\) be the specified map returning the \(Q\)-factor of a QR decomposition. For \(X\in\mathbb{R}_*^{n\times p}\) and \(Y\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times p}\), set \(Q=\operatorname{qf}(X)\) and \(R=Q^TX\), so that \(X=QR\). Then \[\mathrm{D}\operatorname{qf}(X)[Y]=Q\rho_{\mathrm{skew}}(Q^TYR^{-1})+(I_n-QQ^T)YR^{-1},\] where, for \(A=(a_{ij})\), \((\rho_{\mathrm{skew}}(A))_{ij}=a_{ij}\) when \(i>j\), \(0\) when \(i=j\), and \(-a_{ji}\) when \(i<j\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a full-column-rank matrix with the specified QR factorization, the derivative of its Q-factor map is the stated sum of a Q-weighted skew term and an orthogonal-complement term.
assumptions_latex: \(\operatorname{qf}:\mathbb{R}_*^{n\times p}\to\operatorname{St}(p,n)\) is the specified Q-factor map.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathrm{D}\operatorname{qf}(X)[Y]=Q\rho_{\mathrm{skew}}(Q^TYR^{-1})+(I_n-QQ^T)YR^{-1}.\)

children.title: Polar Factorization Kernels
children.top_down_role: Polar-factor kernels used for orthogonality restoration or geometric mapping.

assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\) has full column rank with \(n\ge r\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A=UH\), \(U^\top U=I_r\), and \(H=(A^\top A)^{1/2}\succ0\), uniquely.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Thin polar representation for orthonormalization and projection-type manifold updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The thin polar kernel returns the unique factors \[A=UH,\qquad U^\top U=I_r,\qquad H=(A^\top A)^{1/2}\succ0.\] Equivalently, \(U=A(A^\top A)^{-1/2}\). Thus \(U\) is the orthonormal polar factor associated with \(A\), and it is also the unique closest matrix to \(A\) in the Stiefel set under the Frobenius norm when \(A\) has full column rank.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A full-column-rank matrix has a unique thin polar factorization into an orthonormal factor and a positive-definite symmetric factor.
knowledge_statements.title: Polar Factorization Kernels

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The full-column-rank thin polar factorization and unique Frobenius-nearest Stiefel factor are correct, but the record lacks a polar-decomposition source with a specific locator.

children.title: Singular-Value Decomposition Kernels
children.top_down_role: SVD-based kernels for rank-structured manifold computations.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A=U_r\Sigma_rV_r^\top\) with orthonormal singular vectors and positive singular values.

notation.meaning: diagonal matrix of positive singular values

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compact singular-value decomposition used in low-rank manifold computations.

source_refs.locator: 2.2.5.5. Singular-value decomposition p. 40

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A compact singular-value decomposition kernel returns \[A=U_r\Sigma_rV_r^\top,\qquad U_r^\top U_r=I_r,\qquad V_r^\top V_r=I_r,\] where \(\Sigma_r=\operatorname{diag}(\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_r)\) and \(\sigma_1\ge\cdots\ge\sigma_r>0\). The singular values are unique; singular-vector bases are unique only up to simultaneous orthogonal changes within repeated-singular-value subspaces and matched sign changes for simple singular values.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compact SVD represents a rank-r matrix by orthonormal left and right singular vectors and ordered positive singular values.
knowledge_statements.title: Singular-Value Decomposition Kernels

children.title: Eigendecomposition Kernels
children.top_down_role: Spectral kernels for symmetric, positive-definite, or invariant-subspace structures.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A=Q\Lambda Q^\top\) with \(Q^\top Q=I_n\) and real diagonal \(\Lambda\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Symmetric eigendecomposition for metric operators, Hessian models, and spectral manifold kernels.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A symmetric eigendecomposition kernel returns \[A=Q\Lambda Q^\top,\qquad Q^\top Q=I_n,\qquad \Lambda=\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_n),\] with all \(\lambda_i\in\mathbb R\). The eigenvalues are unique as a multiset. Each simple eigenvector is unique up to sign, while an eigenspace associated with a repeated eigenvalue admits any orthonormal basis. Ordering the diagonal of \(\Lambda\) fixes the eigenvalue order but not these basis freedoms.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every real symmetric matrix has an orthogonal eigendecomposition with real eigenvalues, subject to sign and repeated-eigenspace basis ambiguities.
